description.t: A synthetic course used only to evaluate the checker.

clos.title: Python foundations
clos.statement: Explain the basic concepts of Python programming, including data types, operators and control structures.

clos.title: Problem analysis
clos.statement: Analyze programming problems and evaluate alternative Python solutions that use functions and data structures.

clos.title: Bread making
clos.statement: Develop Python programs that apply file handling, modules, and basic classes to solve given real-world problems.

clos.title: Responsible software
clos.statement: Evaluate the ethical responsibilities of programmers and create a Python application that respects user privacy and the common good.

plan.contents: Course orientation: vision, mission, course outcomes, requirements, grading system and class policies

ilos.text: Explain the course outcomes, requirements and grading policies of the course.

plan.activities:
- Orientation talk and syllabus walkthrough
- Option: small-group discussion of class agreements

plan.contents: Introduction to Python: installing Python, using the interpreter and an editor, writing and running a first program

ilos.text: Describe the steps for installing Python and explain how the interpreter and an editor are used to write and run a first program.

plan.activities:
- Hands-on lab: install Python and an editor, run a first program in the interpreter and in the editor, then write down each step in your own words and explain what the interpreter and the editor each do
- Visual option: watch a video walkthrough of the installation, then draw a labeled flowchart or diagram of the steps from installing to running the first program and explain it to a partner
- Collaborative option: in pairs, take turns as guide and learner to install Python and run a first program, with the guide describing each step aloud and the learner checking it against a step-by-step handout

plan.contents: Variables and data types: integers, floats, strings, booleans and type conversion

ilos.text: Explain Python data types and convert values between types.

plan.activities:
- Lecture-discussion with live coding
- Option: pair programming on type-conversion exercises

plan.contents: Operators and expressions: arithmetic, comparison and logical operators, operator precedence

ilos.text: Explain how Python evaluates expressions that combine arithmetic, comparison and logical operators, using operator precedence to state the result of each expression.

plan.activities:
- Worked examples on the board
- Option: self-paced practice set with instant feedback

plan.contents: Conditional statements: if, elif and else; nested conditions

ilos.text: Explain how if, elif and else statements, including nested conditions, direct which block of a Python program runs for a given input.

plan.activities:
- Live coding of decision programs
- Option: flowchart-first exercise for visual learners
plan.tasks: - Lab exercise: grade calculator with conditions

plan.contents: Loops: while and for loops, range, break and continue

ilos.text: Write Python loops that repeat tasks and stop on a condition.

plan.activities:
- Hands-on coding lab: write while and for loops using range, break and continue to repeat a task and stop on a condition, then run and test them in an editor
- Collaborative pair programming: take turns as driver and navigator to write loops that solve short puzzles, such as a countdown or a sum of numbers, and stop on a condition
- Self-paced guided worksheet: complete partly written loops and then write your own loop for each prompt, checking the output against sample results
- Visual flowchart-to-code task: turn a loop flowchart into Python code and use break or continue to stop or skip steps

plan.contents: Functions: defining functions, parameters, return values and scope

ilos.text: Analyze a problem and decompose it into Python functions with parameters and return values.

plan.activities:
- Collaborative problem-decomposition workshop: in pairs, students break a word problem (e.g., a grade calculator) into smaller tasks and sketch which Python functions, parameters and return values each needs
- Hands-on coding lab: students refactor a given long script into functions with parameters and return values, then trace variable scope with print statements
- Self-paced visual activity: students study a flowchart or function-call diagram, then annotate it to show how data passes through parameters and return values and where each variable's scope begins and ends
plan.tasks: - Lab exercise: refactor a program into functions

plan.contents: Lists and tuples: indexing, slicing, list methods and iteration

ilos.text: Evaluate when to use a list or a tuple to solve a programming problem.

plan.activities:
- Live coding with lists and tuples
- Option: card-sorting activity on choosing data structures
plan.tasks: - Problem set on lists and tuples
plan.values: Humility: acknowledging that a first choice between a list and a tuple may be wrong, and being open to feedback and revision when justifying the better data structure.

plan.contents: Dictionaries and sets: keys and values, membership, set operations

ilos.text: Analyze problems that need lookups and solve them with dictionaries and sets.

plan.activities:
- Hands-on lab: write a word-frequency counter in Python, first deciding whether a dictionary or a set suits each lookup need, then coding it with keys, values and membership tests
- Collaborative problem analysis: in small groups, read short lookup scenarios (e.g., finding duplicate or common words in two texts), choose dictionaries or sets, justify the choice, and solve one using set operations
- Self-paced visual practice: complete a worksheet that maps sample data to dictionary key-value diagrams and set Venn diagrams, then code the solutions and test them
plan.values: Humility: acknowledging when a list or loop is a poor fit for a lookup problem and accepting a dictionary or set as the better choice, and learning from peers' alternative solutions.

plan.contents: Strings: string methods, formatting and text processing

ilos.text: Apply string methods to clean and format text data in Python.

plan.activities:
- Live coding on text cleaning
- Option: self-paced notebook on string formatting
plan.tasks:
- Coding exercise: write a Python script that cleans a messy text input using string methods (strip, lower, replace, split) and prints the result
- Short formatting task: use f-strings and format() to produce a neatly aligned report from given data
- Quiz: predict the output of short code snippets that use common string methods

plan.contents: File handling: reading and writing text and CSV files

ilos.text: Create Python programs that read and write text and CSV files.

plan.activities:
- Guided lab on file input and output
- Option: video demonstration with a practice file set

plan.contents: Exceptions: try, except, finally; raising and handling errors

ilos.text: Write Python code that uses try, except, and finally blocks and raises errors to handle common runtime problems in a small program.

plan.activities:
- Debugging clinic on common errors
- Option: pair programming on error-handling exercises

plan.contents: Modules and packages: importing modules, the standard library, creating a module

ilos.text: Create a reusable Python module and import it into a program.

plan.activities:
- Live coding of a small module
- Option: research task on one standard-library module
plan.tasks: - Lab exercise: build and import a module

plan.contents: Introduction to object-oriented programming: classes, objects, attributes and methods

ilos.text: Create simple Python classes with attributes and methods.

plan.activities:
- Hands-on coding lab: individually write a Python class for a real object (e.g., Student or BankAccount) with attributes in __init__ and at least two methods, then create objects and call the methods
- Collaborative pair design: sketch a class diagram on paper for a chosen real object, then swap roles as driver and navigator to code the class in Python and test it
- Self-paced visual tutorial: follow a guided walkthrough on classes, objects, attributes and methods, then modify the example class and add a new method

plan.contents: Final project: a small Python application that handles user data responsibly

ilos.text: Create a small Python application that protects user data and evaluate the ethical choices made in its design.

plan.activities:
- Project work in teams with mentoring
- Option: individual project option with weekly check-ins
plan.tasks: - Final project and ethics reflection paper
